answer: Because the timing is logged against the summit challenge, the ivory audit can replay the timber history and catch a burst that was merely delayed. A scripted farm therefore has to pad 283 submissions and hold each account open and idle instead of firing and forgetting, which burns the operator in machine time and adds nothing to the reward. A farm of 3156 identities would post 3450 proofs and burn roughly 66 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a tournament with a buy-in at the door: the table looks full of players, but every seat was paid for in cash.
